# Draft:Battle of Göksu

The battle that took place on the Göksu River between the Mongol–Seljuk army led by Badr al-Din Hoteni and Mehmed Bey I of Karaman, following the suppression of the rebellion of Sharaf al-Din Hatiroğlu.”
Background
In the second half of the 13th century, the weakening of the Anatolian Seljuk Sultanate led to increased instability in the region and the rise of various Turkmen principalities. During this period, internal rebellions and conflicts among Seljuk officials and local commanders became more frequent.
One of these uprisings was the rebellion of Sharaf al-Din Hatiroğlu, which further destabilized Seljuk authority in Anatolia. According to some accounts, the Karamanids, who had been in conflict with the Seljuk administration following the death of their founder Karaman Bey, saw the rebellion as an opportunity to expand their influence and supported the uprising.
It is also reported in some sources that Sharaf al-Din Hatiroğlu appointed Mehmed Bey to the administration of the Ermenek region after removing it from Badr al-Din Hoteni, a development which increased tensions in the area.
Following the capture and execution of Sharaf al-Din Hatiroğlu, Badr al-Din Hoteni is said to have gathered a Mongol–Seljuk force and set out to confront Mehmed Bey I of Karaman.
Forces
The exact size of the armies involved in the battle is not known.
In his work, Mahmud al-Aksarayi reports that the Mongol–Seljuk force numbered approximately 2,000 soldiers; however, this figure is not considered definitive by modern historians. In contrast, Ibn Bibi describes the army as considerably larger, without providing a precise number. Meanwhile, the Karamannâme contains much higher and likely exaggerated figures, reflecting the narrative style of the chronicle
rather than verifiable data.
Battle
The battle took place on the Göksu River between the Mongol–Seljuk forces led by Badr al-Din Hoteni and Mehmed Bey I of Karaman.
Following the suppression of the rebellion of Sharaf al-Din Hatiroğlu, tensions in the region escalated, leading to an armed confrontation between the Karamanids and the Mongol–Seljuk administration. According to some accounts, Badr al-Din Hoteni had gathered a Mongol–Seljuk army to confront Mehmed Bey, who had become increasingly influential in the region.
According to some accounts, Badr al-Din Hoteni entered the Göksu River region without adequate reconnaissance, which is suggested as one of the main factors contributing to the Mongol–Seljuk defeat.
It is reported that Mehmed Bey I of Karaman positioned archers along the mountain passes (derbents), allowing the Karamanid forces to launch a coordinated arrow attack as the opposing army arrived. This tactic is described in some sources as causing significant disruption to the Mongol–Seljuk forces at the outset of the engagement.
Following the initial столкновение, the Mongol–Seljuk army reportedly suffered heavy losses and disarray. Badr al-Din Hoteni is said in the sources to have withdrawn from the battlefield, abandoning supplies and military equipment, after which the Karamanid forces secured control of the area.
